correctness.rationale: The explicit radial strong deformation maps every distinct-arm square minus (0,0) to its max-radius-one L boundary, while same-arm triangles contract toward the terminal tip/center configuration. At zero-radius gluing boundaries the formulas coincide and collision remains excluded, so the deformation is simultaneously arm-permutation/particle-exchange equivariant. The retained 2n-vertex n(n−1)-edge connected crown has integral H1=ker ∂ and rank n²−3n+1. On oriented edges arm permutations have trace f(f−1); σ followed by particle exchange reverses exactly 2t2 fixed edges and fixes no graph vertices, giving the two Lefschetz character identities. Half-sum/difference yields Λ² standard and Specht(n−2,2), with n=3 special case. Independently reconstructed a spanning-tree cycle basis and verified both characters for EVERY permutation and particle-swap choice at n=3,4,5,6 (1740 arm permutations, 3480 group tests). Inspected the supplied n≤7 integer cycle checker, but the proof, not finite tests, establishes all n.
residual_risks: Only equilateral arms and two ordered collision-free particles; n=3 lacks the negative Specht summand. The integral lattice is an exact kernel, not a classification into indecomposable modular representations.

value.rationale: The natural automorphism group of an equal-arm star acts on robot-motion homology. The full integral cycle lattice and rational exchange eigenspaces identify exactly which loops persist after forgetting labels and distinguish irreducible arm symmetries. This is a uniform all-n representation classification not implied merely by a previously known Betti rank. It is a motivated exact homological symmetry invariant, not an arbitrary numerical exercise.
residual_risks: The non-equivariant crown reduction is already known; mathematical significance rests on full compatible arm/particle symmetry, not on rediscovering the graph.

limitations: No claim for >2 particles, non-equilateral arm group, arbitrary graph, modular indecomposable decomposition, or equivariant stable homotopy.
Known ordered metric-star model is credited and is a prerequisite.
